note: A token the provider refused stays refused until a refresh succeeds, though its expiry looks fresh.
A late refusal of an older token is answered with its replacement only while the replacement is still fresh.
A reply with a duplicate key is malformed in both implementations; Go kept the last authMethod and Swift the first.
authMethod "" is a mode that is not chatgpt; only null (or absence) is not-signed-in.
A refresh reply that names another sign-in is classified as that sign-in, not as expired (sequence step 4).
A vertical tab is not JSON whitespace: the line is malformed in both implementations.
U+00A0 is not JSON whitespace: the line is malformed (Go's bytes.TrimSpace used to remove it).
An error code beyond the signed 64-bit range is malformed; it must not wrap to -32601 and lead to config/read.
A message with an id and a method, even "", is a server request: refused, never taken as the reply to call 2.
A notification is ignored whatever else it holds; its reply fields are never read.
A last reply ended by EOF rather than a newline is still a line, as Go's bufio.Scanner reads it.
A number beyond a float64 (1e999) makes the line malformed even in a field nobody reads: Foundation refuses it wherever it is, and Codex's serde refuses it too.
A message without an id is a notification and is ignored whatever else it holds, a method that is not a string included.
The version is the digits and dots after the first slash, read as bytes: a combining mark after a digit ends it (0.162), as in Go, rather than making the whole part non-numeric.
Codex answering the token call with -32601 (updated between the two calls) takes the same config/read rule as the metadata call.
A refresh answered with -32601 takes the config/read rule too: the store is the file, so its fresh token is used, and it is not refreshed again.
The token Codex hands out carries the account it names.
